evals.name: topic-action-runs-mission-interview
evals.expected_output: Routes to the topic action (start-or-resume). For a new rust-ownership workspace it creates the workspace and runs the mission interview (WHY, goal, success criteria) before teaching; if one already exists it resumes from saved state. Either way it opens with orientation, not a lecture dump.
expectations: Routes to the `topic` action and resolves the workspace under the plugin data dir (not the consuming repo)
For a new workspace, runs the mission interview (WHY / goal / success) before teaching; for an existing one, resumes from saved state rather than re-interviewing from scratch
Does not open by lecturing content before the mission is established or prior state is loaded

evals.name: smart-default-detects-codebase-vs-topic
evals.prompt: /teach:teach the auth-flow module in this repo
evals.expected_output: With no explicit action and a subject naming a repo-grounded concept, resolves to codebase mode and grounds in files discovered at teach-time; if discovery finds no real grounding for the concept in this repo, it asks the user to point to the relevant area rather than inventing repo sources.
expectations: Detects that the subject names a repo-grounded concept and resolves to `codebase` mode (not `topic`)
Discovers grounding from live repo files at teach-time (climbs for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, surveys structure) rather than baked assumptions
If no real grounding for the concept is found in the repo, asks the user to point to the relevant area instead of inventing or hallucinating repo sources

evals.name: primer-creates-no-workspace
evals.prompt: /teach:teach primer color-grading — I just need enough vocabulary to direct the work now.
evals.expected_output: Runs the single-session primer with NO workspace, glossary, or learning records. It first intakes the user's starting point with one question, then builds the vocabulary ladder (terms, quality axes, good-vs-bad examples, a prompt template).
expectations: Creates NO workspace directory, glossary, or learning records for the primer (single-session, no persistence)

Opens by intaking the user's starting point with one question, then builds the vocabulary ladder — core terms, the quality axes experts judge by, worked good-vs-bad examples, and a closing prompt template
Offers to escalate to `/teach:teach topic color-grading` for depth rather than silently starting a full workspace

evals.name: coach-one-question-at-a-time
evals.prompt: /teach:teach topic binary-search-trees — I want to understand how deletion works.
evals.expected_output: Adopts coach posture from the first turn: opens with a single question (the mission interview for a new workspace, or a teaching-dialog question in an active one), asks one question at a time, and never opens by lecturing the whole deletion algorithm.
expectations: Opens with ONE question and waits, rather than front-loading a full explanation
Leads with questions before explanations, per coach-not-lecturer posture (the mission interview itself is one-question-at-a-time)
Does not dump the complete deletion algorithm in a single lecture turn

evals.name: ground-in-primary-sources-not-recall
evals.expected_output: For a new workspace it runs the mission interview before teaching; and whenever it teaches the Knowledge layer for this fast-moving framework, it grounds claims in primary sources fetched or files Read this turn (RESOURCES.md / official docs), never parametric recall, since library/framework facts drift.
expectations: Respects the new-workspace flow — runs the mission interview / resource seeding before delivering Knowledge content, rather than jumping straight into framework facts
Any Knowledge-layer claim that drives a lesson is grounded in a source fetched or a file Read this turn, not training-data recall
Does not assert volatile framework facts from memory — pulls from RESOURCES.md / documentation sources for this fast-moving topic

evals.name: no-silent-workspace-invention
evals.expected_output: The explain action requires an active workspace to write concepts/<concept>/ into, and never silently invents one. It resolves against the live workspace state: uses the single existing workspace when exactly one exists, asks which when several exist, and asks whether to start one (topic/codebase) when none exists — so the correct behavior depends on the current workspace state rather than being a fixed branch.
expectations: Recognizes that `explain` requires an active workspace to write concepts/<concept>/ into
Never silently invents or fabricates a workspace — it resolves against the live existing workspace state before writing
Takes the branch that matches the current state: use the one existing workspace, ask which when several exist, or ask whether to start one when none exists
